claim: Drosophila tracheal progenitors are adult stem cells that migrate posteriorly along the dorsal trunk to replenish degenerating branches.
source: Drosophila tracheal progenitors are adult stem cells that migrate posteriorly along the dorsal trunk to replenish degenerating branches that disperse the fibroblast growth factor mitogen.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known characteristic of the system being studied.

claim: Individual tracheal progenitor cells migrate together in a concerted, disciplined manner.
source: Here, we show that individual progenitor cells migrate together in a concerted, disciplined manner, a behavior that is dependent on the neighboring fat body.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental observations throughout the manuscript.

claim: The disciplined migration of tracheal progenitors is dependent on the neighboring fat body.
source: Here, we show that individual progenitor cells migrate together in a concerted, disciplined manner, a behavior that is dependent on the neighboring fat body.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through fat body depletion experiments.

claim: Fat body-derived cytokine Upd2 targets and induces JAK/STAT signaling in tracheal progenitors to maintain their directional migration.
source: We identify the fat body-derived cytokine, Upd2, in targeting and inducing JAK/STAT signaling in tracheal progenitors to maintain their directional migration.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by genetic and molecular experiments.

claim: Perturbation of Upd2 production in fat body causes aberrant bidirectional migration of tracheal progenitors.
source: Perturbation of either Upd2 production in fat body or JAK/STAT signaling in trachea causes aberrant bidirectional migration of tracheal progenitors.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through RNAi experiments.

claim: Perturbation of JAK/STAT signaling in trachea causes aberrant bidirectional migration of tracheal progenitors.
source: Perturbation of either Upd2 production in fat body or JAK/STAT signaling in trachea causes aberrant bidirectional migration of tracheal progenitors.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through genetic and pharmacological experiments.

claim: JAK/STAT signaling promotes the expression of genes involved in planar cell polarity.
source: We show that JAK/STAT signaling promotes the expression of genes involved in planar cell polarity leading to asymmetric localization of Fat in progenitor cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by ChIP-seq and expression analysis.

claim: JAK/STAT signaling leads to asymmetric localization of Fat in progenitor cells.
source: We show that JAK/STAT signaling promotes the expression of genes involved in planar cell polarity leading to asymmetric localization of Fat in progenitor cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through imaging experiments.

claim: Upd2 transport requires Rab5- and Rab7-mediated endocytic sorting.
source: We provide evidence that Upd2 transport requires Rab5- and Rab7-mediated endocytic sorting and Lbm-dependent vesicle trafficking.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by genetic and imaging experiments.

claim: Upd2 transport requires Lbm-dependent vesicle trafficking.
source: We provide evidence that Upd2 transport requires Rab5- and Rab7-mediated endocytic sorting and Lbm-dependent vesicle trafficking.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by genetic and imaging experiments.

claim: Tracheal progenitors reside in Tr4 and Tr5 metameres and start to move along the tracheal branch toward sites of regeneration.
source: The progenitor cells reside in Tr4 and Tr5 metameres and start to move along the tracheal branch toward sites of regeneration (Chen and Krasnow, 2014; Pitsouli and Perrimon, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Movement of tracheal progenitor cells follows a stereotypical anterior-to-posterior axis.
source: Movement of these progenitor cells follows a stereotypical anterior-to-posterior axis (Figure 1A), thus representing a suitable system to investigate mechanisms controlling the directionality of stem cell migration.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The activation of tracheal progenitors is stimulated by the morphogen Branchless (Bnl), fly homolog of fibroblast growth factor (FGF).
source: The activation of tracheal progenitors is stimulated by the morphogen Branchless (Bnl), fly homolog of fibroblast growth factor (FGF) (Chen and Krasnow, 2014), and the insulin hormone (Li et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The activation of tracheal progenitors is stimulated by the insulin hormone.
source: The activation of tracheal progenitors is stimulated by the morphogen Branchless (Bnl), fly homolog of fibroblast growth factor (FGF) (Chen and Krasnow, 2014), and the insulin hormone (Li et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Drosophila fat body is the functional analog of mammalian adipose tissue.
source: Drosophila fat body is the functional analog of mammalian adipose tissue and the major organ sensing various hormonal and nutritional signals to orchestrate systemic growth, metabolism and stem cell maintenance (Sriskanthadevan-Pirahas et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: Fat body produces regulatory molecules known as fat body signals (FBSs), which remotely affect the activity of other organs.
source: Fat body produces regulatory molecules known as fat body signals (FBSs), which remotely affect the activity of other organs (Ingaramo et al., 2020; Zheng et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The fat body resides anatomically in proximity with trachea.
source: In Drosophila, the fat body resides anatomically in proximity with trachea (Figure 1B, C; Video 1) and is the principal reservoir for energy consumption.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1B, C and Video 1.

claim: Expression of hid and rpr in L3 stage impaired fat body integrity and adipocyte abundance, and generated slender larvae and pupae.
source: Expression of hid and rpr in L3 stage impaired fat body integrity and adipocyte abundance, and generated slender larvae and pupae (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: In fat body-defective animals, tracheal progenitors exhibited undisciplined migration and tended to move bidirectionally.
source: In these animals, the tracheal progenitors exhibited a sign of undisciplined migration and tended to move bidirectionally (Figure 1D–F), although their migration rate, cell number and proliferation remained unchanged (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–H, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by multiple figures.

claim: Migration rate, cell number and proliferation of tracheal progenitors remained unchanged in fat body-defective animals.
source: In these animals, the tracheal progenitors exhibited a sign of undisciplined migration and tended to move bidirectionally (Figure 1D–F), although their migration rate, cell number and proliferation remained unchanged (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–H, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by supplementary figures.

claim: Entropy of the tracheal progenitor migration system was notably elevated upon increased inconsistency of migration vectors in fat body-depleted animals.
source: Owing to this undisciplined movement, entropy of the system was notably elevated upon increased inconsistency of migration vectors (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1K showing quantitative analysis.

claim: RNA sequencing analysis revealed a dramatical alteration of transcriptional program in tracheal progenitors upon the perturbation of fat body.
source: The results revealed a dramatical alteration of transcriptional program in tracheal progenitors upon the perturbation of fat body (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B, B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by RNA-seq data in supplementary figures.

claim: The functional cluster of 'cytokine activity' showed prominent enrichment in the differentially expressed genes in progenitors from lsp2>rpr.hid pupae.
source: Interestingly, the functional cluster of 'cytokine activity' showed prominent enrichment in the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in progenitors from lsp2>rpr.hid pupae (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2A showing GO analysis.

claim: The cytokine-dependent JAK/STAT and Dpp signaling were notably upregulated upon the activation of progenitors.
source: Analyzing the RNA-seq data revealed that the cytokine-dependent JAK/STAT and Dpp signaling were notably upregulated upon the activation of progenitors (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2B showing heatmap analysis.

claim: Fat body depletion led to suppression of target genes of JAK/STAT, PI3K, and Dpp signaling in tracheal progenitors.
source: Importantly, fat body depletion led to suppression of target genes of JAK/STAT, PI3K, and Dpp signaling in tracheal progenitors, suggesting their dependence on the function of fat body (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2C showing heatmap analysis.

claim: Knockdown of upd2 in fat body phenocopied fat body ablation-induced bidirectional movement of tracheal progenitors.
source: Knockdown of candidates including some cytokines specifically in fat body did not affect the direction of tracheal progenitor migration (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–J), except for upd2, whose depletion phenocopied fat body ablation-induced bidirectional movement of tracheal progenitors (Figure 2D–F and Video 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2D–F and Video 3.

claim: Domeless (Dome), the receptor for JAK/STAT pathway, exhibited pronounced expression in the tracheal progenitors.
source: Domeless (Dome), the receptor for JAK/STAT pathway, exhibited pronounced expression in the tracheal progenitors (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claim: The DIPF reporter displayed robust fluorescent signal in the tracheal progenitors.
source: When expressed in the tracheal system, DIPF displayed robust fluorescent signal in the tracheal progenitors (Figure 2J).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2J showing confocal imaging.

claim: Perturbation of Dome, Hop, or Stat92E by btl-Gal4-driven expression of RNAi constructs caused tracheal progenitors to aberrantly migrate anteriorly.
source: To analyze the functional importance of JAK/STAT signaling in tracheal progenitors, we perturbed the principal components of this signaling, namely the receptor Dome, signal transducer Hop, or the downstream transcription factor Stat92E, by btl-Gal4-driven expression of RNAi constructs. Under these conditions in which JAK/STAT pathway is compromised, the tracheal progenitors aberrantly migrated anteriorly, which is reminiscent of upd2 loss-of-function in the fat body (Figure 3A–E, Video 4, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by multiple figures and videos.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of JAK by Tofacitinib triggered bidirectional movement of tracheal progenitors.
source: In agreement with genetic perturbation of JAK/STAT signaling, pharmacological inhibition of JAK by a small-molecule inhibitor, Tofacitinib (Palmroth et al., 2021), also triggered bidirectional movement of tracheal progenitors (Figure 3F–H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3F–H.

claim: The aberrant anterior migration of tracheal progenitors upon perturbation of JAK/STAT components led to incomplete regeneration of airway and impairment of tracheal integrity and caused melanization in the trachea.
source: The aberrant anterior migration of tracheal progenitors upon perturbation of JAK/STAT components led to incomplete regeneration of airway and impairment of tracheal integrity and caused melanization in the trachea (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–I.

claim: Stat92E binding was detected in the promoters and intronic regions of genes functioning in distal-to-proximal signaling, such as dachsous (ds), four-jointed (fj), fz, stan, Vang, and fat2.
source: Notably, Stat92E binding was detected in the promoters and intronic regions of genes functioning in distal-to-proximal signaling (Cho and Irvine, 2004), such as dachsous (ds), four-jointed (fj), fz, stan, Vang, and fat2 (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4C showing ChIP-seq peaks.

claim: Ds and Fj were abundant in the progenitor cells, but were vastly reduced upon depletion of dome, hop, or stat92E.
source: Ds and Fj were abundant in the progenitor cells, but were vastly reduced upon depletion of dome, hop, or stat92E, suggesting that they are regulated by JAK/STAT pathway (Figure 4D–M).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4D–M showing expression analysis.

claim: The level of Ft was elevated by the reduction of JAK/STAT signaling.
source: Furthermore, it is reported that the function of Ft is influenced by cell-autonomous increase of Ds level and its protein level is enhanced by Ds reduction (Ambegaonkar et al., 2012; Matakatsu and Blair, 2004), which is also evidenced by our analysis using dsRNAi and UAS-ds in the tracheal progenitors (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–D). In accordance with this notion, the level of Ft, as assayed by the Ft-GFP reporter, was elevated by the reduction of JAK/STAT signaling (Figure 4N–R).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4N–R and citations.

claim: Tracheal progenitors exhibited bidirectional movement when ds, ft, or fj were perturbed by RNAi expression.
source: To evaluate the functional roles of the polarity proteins in tracheal progenitor migration, we perturbed their expression in the tracheal progenitors by expressing RNAi against ds, ft, or fj, which were identified by ChIP-seq as the targets of JAK/STAT. In these flies, tracheal progenitors exhibited bidirectional movement, which is reminiscent of the impairment of JAK/STAT signaling (Figure 5A–E and Video 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5A–E and Video 5.

claim: Both loss- and gain-of-function of PCP components disrupt the PCP.
source: Similar observations were obtained by over-expression of ft or ds in the trachea (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D), consistent with previous reports that both loss- and gain-of-function of PCP components disrupt the PCP (Adler et al., 2000; Tree et al., 2002; Vinson and Adler, 1987).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations and experimental data.

claim: Normal posteriorly migrating tracheal progenitors extend protrusions toward the migratory directions.
source: The normal posteriorly migrating tracheal progenitors extend protrusions toward the migratory directions (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), but in the bidirectionally moving progenitors in which upd2 in fat body was perturbed, extensive filopodia were projected from both the anterior and posterior fronts (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B, C), indicating that the aberrantly anteriorly moving progenitors may adopt the identity as those moving posteriorly.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: In bidirectionally moving progenitors in which upd2 in fat body was perturbed, extensive filopodia were projected from both the anterior and posterior fronts.
source: The normal posteriorly migrating tracheal progenitors extend protrusions toward the migratory directions (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), but in the bidirectionally moving progenitors in which upd2 in fat body was perturbed, extensive filopodia were projected from both the anterior and posterior fronts (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B, C), indicating that the aberrantly anteriorly moving progenitors may adopt the identity as those moving posteriorly.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 2B, C.

claim: Progenitors exhibited elevated levels of Ft at the leading edge where they attached to DT.
source: Further analysis revealed that the progenitors exhibited elevated levels of Ft at the leading edge where they attached to DT (Figure 5F, G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5F, G showing imaging analysis.

claim: Progenitors that underwent bidirectional movement exhibited pronounced abundance of Ft at both the anterior and posterior frontal edges.
source: Accordingly, progenitors that underwent bidirectional movement exhibited pronounced abundance of Ft at both the anterior and posterior frontal edges (Figure 5H–J).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5H–J showing imaging analysis.

claim: Administration of L3 larvae with Brefeldin A (BFA) sequestered Upd2 proteins in fat body.
source: In agreement with Upd2 being transported through vesicles, administration of L3 larvae with Brefeldin A (BFA), which pharmacologically inhibits vesicle formation and transport, sequestered Upd2 proteins in fat body (Figure 6B, C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6B, C showing imaging data.

claim: Considerable amount of Upd2 puncta were detected in the tracheal progenitors.
source: To track the destination of the Upd2-containing vesicles, we examined mCherry signals in adjacent tissues and detected considerable amount of Upd2 puncta in the tracheal progenitors (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6D showing imaging data.

claim: BFA treatment reduced Upd2-mCherry puncta in the tracheal progenitors.
source: BFA treatment reduced Upd2-mCherry puncta in the tracheal progenitors, suggesting that tracheal progenitors receive vesicular Upd2 from the fat body (Figure 6E, F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6E, F showing quantitative imaging data.

claim: Perturbation of Grasp65 led to sequestration of Upd2-containing vesicles in fat body.
source: Perturbation of Grasp65, a Golgi reassembly stacking protein previously implicated in Upd2 secretion (Rajan et al., 2017), also led to sequestration of Upd2-containing vesicles in fat body (Figure 6G, H, J).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6G, H, J and citation.

claim: When expressing lbmRNAi in fat body, Upd2-containing vesicles were vastly increased.
source: When expressing lbmRNAi in fat body, Upd2-containing vesicles were vastly increased (Figure 6I, J).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6I, J showing quantitative imaging data.

claim: Perturbation of vesicle secretion or transport by expressing grasp65RNAi or lbmRNAi in fat body eliminated the presence of fat body-origin Upd2 in the trachea.
source: Meanwhile, perturbation of vesicle secretion or transport by expressing grasp65RNAi or lbmRNAi in fat body eliminated the presence of fat body-origin Upd2 in the trachea, suggesting that fat body-produced Upd2-containing vesicles function cell non-autonomously and contribute to other tissues/organs (Figure 6K–N).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6K–N showing imaging data.

claim: Knockdown of upd2 in the trachea did not alter the discipline of tracheal progenitor migration.
source: It should be noted that knockdown of upd2 in the trachea did not alter the discipline of tracheal progenitor migration (Figure 2—figure supplement 1K–M).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1K–M.

claim: Expression of grasp65RNAi in fat body reduced the activity of JAK/STAT signaling in the trachea.
source: Expression of grasp65RNAi in fat body reduced the activity of JAK/STAT signaling in the trachea, as assessed by the Stat92E-GFP reporter (Figure 7A, B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7A, B showing reporter expression.

claim: RNAi targeting expression of lbm in fat body vanished JAK/STAT signal transduction in the trachea.
source: Similarly, RNAi targeting expression of lbm in fat body vanished JAK/STAT signal transduction in the trachea (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7C showing reporter expression.

claim: Knockdown of rab5 or rab7 in fat body reduced the activity of JAK/STAT signaling in the progenitor cells.
source: Consistently, knockdown of rab5 or rab7 in fat body reduced the activity of JAK/STAT signaling in the progenitor cells (Figure 7D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7D–F showing reporter expression.

claim: BFA treatment that impeded vesicular transport resulted in impairment of JAK/STAT signaling in trachea.
source: Corroborating the genetic manipulations, BFA treatment that impeded vesicular transport also resulted in impairment of JAK/STAT signaling in trachea (Figure 7G–I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7G–I showing reporter expression.

claim: The fluorescent signal of DIPF was compromised upon the presence of BFA.
source: Taking advantage of the aforementioned DIPF reporter to assess the response of receiving cells to ligands, we found that the fluorescent signal of DIPF was compromised upon the presence of BFA, but was unaffected by inhibitors that target the downstream JAK protein (Figure 7J–M), suggesting that signaling ligands are less abundant in the recipient progenitor cells and that the vesicle-mediated transport of ligands is essential for JAK/STAT signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7J–M showing reporter analysis.

claim: The fluorescent signal of DIPF was unaffected by inhibitors that target the downstream JAK protein.
source: Taking advantage of the aforementioned DIPF reporter to assess the response of receiving cells to ligands, we found that the fluorescent signal of DIPF was compromised upon the presence of BFA, but was unaffected by inhibitors that target the downstream JAK protein (Figure 7J–M), suggesting that signaling ligands are less abundant in the recipient progenitor cells and that the vesicle-mediated transport of ligands is essential for JAK/STAT signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7J–M showing reporter analysis.

claim: Tracheal progenitors exhibited bidirectional migration in BFA-treated flies.
source: Phenotypically, the tracheal progenitors exhibited bidirectional migration in BFA-treated flies, which phenocopies JAK/STAT loss-of-function (Figure 7N–P).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7N–P showing migration analysis.

claim: Depletion of grasp65 or lbm led to bidirectional movement of tracheal progenitors.
source: In concord with this observation, depletion of grasp65 or lbm also led to bidirectional movement (Figure 7Q–S'', and Video 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7Q–S'' and Video 6.

claim: Perturbation of neither rab2 nor rab3 affected the disciplined progenitor migration.
source: Similar observations were made in tracheal progenitors with either rab5 or rab7 knockdown (Figure 7T–V), whereas perturbation of neither rab2 nor rab3 affected the disciplined progenitor migration (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: Both Rab5 and Rab7 were found adjacent to the Upd2-harboring vesicles.
source: The fat body-produced Upd2 appeared vesicular (Figure 8A) and both Rab5 and Rab7 were found adjacent to the Upd2-harboring vesicles, suggesting that both Rab GTPases function in the transport of Upd2 (Figure 8A'–B'').
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8A'–B'' showing colocalization imaging.

claim: Grasp65 was in close proximity to Upd2-containing vesicles.
source: Furthermore, we observed that Grasp65 was in close proximity to Upd2-containing vesicles, indicating its integral roles in these vesicles (Figure 8C–C'').
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8C–C'' showing colocalization imaging.

claim: Upd2 was observed to colocalize with the tetraspanin, Lbm.
source: In addition, Upd2 was observed to colocalize with the tetraspanin, Lbm (Figure 8D–D'').
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8D–D'' showing colocalization imaging.

claim: Proximity ligation assay revealed strong interactions between Upd2 and Rab5, Rab7, and Lbm.
source: To determine if Upd2 interacts with the coordinators of vesicle trafficking, we employed the Duolink in situ proximity ligation assay (PLA) which revealed strong interactions between Upd2 and Rabs, such as Rab5 and Rab7 (Figure 8E–H), as well as Lbm (Figure 8I, J).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8E–J showing PLA results.

claim: Upd2 co-immunoprecipitated with Rab5 and Rab7.
source: The interaction was further validated by the revelation that Upd2 co-immunoprecipitated with Rab5 and Rab7 (Figure 8K, L).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8K, L showing co-IP results.

claim: Lbm physically associated with Upd2 in both fat body and S2 cells.
source: The presence of Upd2 in Lbm-containing vesicles was also evidenced in S2 cells (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A–C'') and co-IP experiment showed that Lbm physically associated with Upd2 in both fat body and S2 cells (Figure 8M, Figure 8—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8M and Figure 8—figure supplement 1F showing co-IP results.

claim: Fat body expressing Lbm-pHluorin produced GFP puncta at the plasma membrane.
source: Fat body expressing Lbm-pHluorin produced GFP puncta at the plasma membrane (Figure 8N), and the GFP signal was also detected in the trachea, suggesting the reception and internalization of Lbm-containing vesicles by tracheal cells (Figure 8O).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8N showing imaging data.

claim: GFP signal from Lbm-pHluorin was detected in the trachea, suggesting the reception and internalization of Lbm-containing vesicles by tracheal cells.
source: Fat body expressing Lbm-pHluorin produced GFP puncta at the plasma membrane (Figure 8N), and the GFP signal was also detected in the trachea, suggesting the reception and internalization of Lbm-containing vesicles by tracheal cells (Figure 8O).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8O showing imaging data.

claim: The signals of Lbm-pHluorin in both fat body and responding tracheoblasts were apparently compromised when Rab5 or Rab7 was perturbed.
source: Accordingly, the signals of Lbm-pHluorin in both fat body and responding tracheoblasts were apparently compromised when Rab5 or Rab7 was perturbed (Figure 8P–S), suggesting that the biogenesis and production of Lbm-containing vesicles depend on Rab-mediated vesicle trafficking.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8P–S showing imaging data.

claim: JAK/STAT signaling does not serve as a guidance cue for tracheal progenitors, but rather directs the directionality of cell movement.
source: Our results suggest that JAK/STAT signaling does not serve as a guidance cue for tracheal progenitors, but rather directs the directionality of cell movement.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the results.

claim: The Drosophila family of interleukin-6 (IL-6)-like cytokines consist of Unpaired (Upd, also called Outstretched), Upd2 and Upd3.
source: The Drosophila family of interleukin-6 (IL-6)-like cytokines consist of Unpaired (Upd, also called Outstretched), Upd2 and Upd3, and serve as mediators of systemic signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as background knowledge.

claim: Upd2 is primarily produced by the fat body.
source: Whereas Upd1 and Upd3 derive from fly brain and plasmatocytes (Beshel et al., 2017; Woodcock et al., 2015), Upd2 is primarily produced by the fat body (Rajan et al., 2017), although muscle-derived Upd2 is also reported (Zhao and Karpac, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The Upd proteins act as ligands which bind to a common GP130-like receptor, Domeless (Dome) on target cells.
source: The Upd proteins act as ligands which bind to a common GP130-like receptor, Domeless (Dome) on target cells (Agaisse et al., 2003; Chen et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Upon association of ligands, the Dome receptors dimerize and recruit the non-receptor tyrosine kinase JAKs leading to their subsequent transactivation via phosphorylation.
source: Upon association of ligands, the Dome receptors dimerize and recruit the non-receptor tyrosine kinase JAKs leading to their subsequent transactivation via phosphorylation.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as background knowledge about JAK/STAT signaling.

claim: The transactivated JAKs phosphorylate the tyrosine residues of their substrates, including the bound receptors and cytosolic STATs.
source: The transactivated JAKs then phosphorylate the tyrosine residues of their substrates, including the bound receptors and cytosolic STATs.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as background knowledge about JAK/STAT signaling.

claim: The phosphorylation of STATs promotes their dimerization and nuclear translocation to activate transcriptional program.
source: The phosphorylation of STATs promotes their dimerization and nuclear translocation to activate transcriptional program (Darnell, 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with supporting citation.

claim: IL-6 cytokines tend to be encapsulated in secretory vesicles.
source: It has been reported that IL-6 cytokines tend to be encapsulated in secretory vesicles (Kandere-Grzybowska et al., 2003; Verboogen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: Tetraspanins facilitate regeneration and wound healing in cultural cells and single-cell plasma membrane.
source: It has been proposed that tetraspanins facilitate regeneration and wound healing in cultural cells and single-cell plasma membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as background knowledge.

claim: Tetraspanin-enriched macrodomains are assembled into a ring-like structure which is recruited to large membrane wounds and promotes membrane repair.
source: Tetraspanin-enriched macrodomains are assembled into a ring-like structure (Huang et al., 2022), which is recruited to large membrane wounds and promotes membrane repair (Wang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: The vesicle-mediated transport of ligands is essential for JAK/STAT signaling.
source: Taking advantage of the aforementioned DIPF reporter to assess the response of receiving cells to ligands, we found that the fluorescent signal of DIPF was compromised upon the presence of BFA, but was unaffected by inhibitors that target the downstream JAK protein (Figure 7J–M), suggesting that signaling ligands are less abundant in the recipient progenitor cells and that the vesicle-mediated transport of ligands is essential for JAK/STAT signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of experimental data.

claim: The biogenesis and production of Lbm-containing vesicles depend on Rab-mediated vesicle trafficking.
source: Accordingly, the signals of Lbm-pHluorin in both fat body and responding tracheoblasts were apparently compromised when Rab5 or Rab7 was perturbed (Figure 8P–S), suggesting that the biogenesis and production of Lbm-containing vesicles depend on Rab-mediated vesicle trafficking.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of experimental data.

claim: Fat body-derived Upd2 interacts with Rab-mediated endocytic trafficking system to control the disciplined movement of tracheal progenitors.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that fat body-derived Upd2 interacts with Rab-mediated endocytic trafficking system to control the disciplined movement of tracheal progenitors.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary interpretation of multiple experiments.

claim: Tracheal progenitors establish migratory directionality as they exit their niches.
source: Our study reveals that tracheal progenitors establish migratory directionality as they exit their niches and that the disciplined migration of the progenitors depends on an inter-organ signaling originating from the fat body.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as a summary of the study's findings.

claim: The disciplined migration of the progenitors depends on an inter-organ signaling originating from the fat body.
source: Our study reveals that tracheal progenitors establish migratory directionality as they exit their niches and that the disciplined migration of the progenitors depends on an inter-organ signaling originating from the fat body.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as a summary of the study's findings.

claim: Approximately 95.7% of Stat92E binding peaks located within 2 kb of transcription start sites of annotated genes.
source: This revealed a total of 21,312 Stat92E binding peaks, ~95.7% of which located within 2 kb of transcription start sites of annotated genes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 86% of the Stat92E binding peaks (18,328 peaks) were enriched either in promoter regions or within gene bodies.
source: In particular, 86% of the peaks (18,328 peaks) were enriched either in promoter regions or within gene bodies, and 66.1% of the peaks (13,490 peaks) resided near the 5ʹ ends of annotated genes, namely in the promoter regions, first exons and first introns (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: 66.1% of the Stat92E binding peaks (13,490 peaks) resided near the 5ʹ ends of annotated genes.
source: In particular, 86% of the peaks (18,328 peaks) were enriched either in promoter regions or within gene bodies, and 66.1% of the peaks (13,490 peaks) resided near the 5ʹ ends of annotated genes, namely in the promoter regions, first exons and first introns (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, C.
